title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were not designed to handle sustained periods of heavy traffic congestion, and a large number of them became immobilized when their batteries drained during gridlock following Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco. The vehicles remained stationary on streets near the Golden Gate Bridge for hours while waiting for roadside assistance to tow them away. This is a failure to anticipate and design for foreseeable operating conditions in a dense urban environment during a predictable peak traffic event.

The deployment lacked sufficient safeguards for battery management during traffic delays. A system operating in a city should have included either the capacity to reserve battery reserves for movement out of congestion, alerts to human operators to preposition vehicles before predicted traffic spikes, or restrictions on accepting rides when traffic forecasting suggested prolonged delays. The incident was compounded by reports of at least one vehicle continuing to drive during fireworks and another catching fire after driving over fireworks debris, suggesting the vehicles were not withdrawn from service despite clearly hazardous conditions.

It is not established whether Waymo had received warnings about Fourth of July traffic or chose not to act on them, or whether the company had previously identified this vulnerability and deprioritized fixing it.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Several Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets after their batteries drained during severe traffic congestion following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations on Saturday. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets near the Golden Gate Bridge. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures. Waymo's roadside assistance team worked to tow the vehicles away, and the company stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during heavy traffic situations.

The incident highlighted challenges autonomous vehicles face in unexpected conditions. One passenger reported a Waymo vehicle continued driving during fireworks, and a vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks with no injuries reported. Frustrated motorists complained about the stationary cars blocking traffic for hours. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss Saturday night's traffic experience with stakeholders to ensure smoother outcomes for future events. The city previously experienced issues with Waymo vehicles during a December power outage that affected traffic lights.
